content:
Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness
[![unit tests](https://github.com/YUNTONGDONG/opsflow-agent-harness/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/YUNTONGDONG/opsflow-agent-harness/actions/workflows/test.yml)

A reliable agent harness for knowledge retrieval and operational workflow
automation. It separates model-driven request understanding from deterministic
execution, state management, recovery, and evidence collection.

OpsFlow is not primarily a LangChain chatbot. LangChain is used at the model
boundary for prompt and structured-output integration. The OpsFlow Harness
owns the execution contract: skill discovery, validated plans, dependency-aware
scheduling, bounded retries, write safety, durable state, workspace evidence,
and request-level traces.

> The model understands and plans. The Harness controls state and execution.
> Skills perform business operations.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Why an Agent Harness?
A model can choose a tool or produce a plan, but a production agent still needs
deterministic answers to operational questions:

- Is the requested skill registered and is its input valid?
- Which steps can run concurrently, and which depend on earlier output?
- Is a failed operation safe to retry?
- Did an external write complete when the response timed out?
- How does an interrupted task resume without repeating side effects?
- Where are the request, plan, step evidence, and correlated trace stored?

The Harness implements these controls outside the model loop so that they can be
tested, inspected, and recovered independently.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Architecture
All entry points use the same runtime factory and the same Harness execution
path:

```text
Slack / REST API / Local CLI
              |
              v
         HarnessAgent
              |
              v
      HarnessApplication
              |
              v
   Router / Planner (structured output)
              |
              v
          TaskRunner
              |
              v
         SkillRuntime
              |
              v
Knowledge / Log / Web / Calendar / Tasks Skills

Harness <------> Redis task, session, and profile state
Runtime/Skills <-> Workspace request and step evidence
All stages ------> Correlated Trace events
```

The default runtime is selected explicitly:

```env
AGENT_RUNTIME=harness
```

The legacy `AgentClass` remains available only as an explicit migration fallback
with `AGENT_RUNTIME=legacy`; it is not the default path for REST, Slack, or CLI
requests.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Harness Responsibilities > Registry and validated routing
The Skill Registry exposes canonical names, operation types, and input schemas.
The Router produces a structured route or plan constrained by that registry.
Pydantic validation and runtime lookup reject unknown skills and invalid inputs
before business code executes.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Harness Responsibilities > Dependency-aware execution
`TaskRunner` validates step identifiers, dependencies, cycles, and `$from`
output bindings. Independent read steps can run concurrently within configured
global and per-skill limits. Writes remain serial, and a failed dependency
blocks downstream work.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Harness Responsibilities > Read and write safety
Only declared read operations receive bounded automatic retries. Writes use
idempotency records and external-state verification. If the external result
cannot be determined, the step becomes `UNKNOWN`; recovery verifies the
external system instead of blindly repeating the write.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Harness Responsibilities > Recovery and evidence
Tasks persist step state and external resource identifiers. Interrupted reads
can resume, while uncertain writes are reverified. Request inputs, plans, step
inputs and outputs, and final responses are saved to the Workspace. Trace events
correlate the full request with `request_id`, `task_id`, and `step_id`.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Included Skills
The Harness registers the following production skill contracts:

- `knowledge_search`: FAISS Top-100 recall, SVMRank Top-20 filtering, and
  Cross-Encoder Top-3 reranking before evidence-grounded answer generation.
- `log_diagnosis`: analyzes supplied log text or queries a configured log API.
- `web_search`: delegates live search to the configured backend.
- `calendar_management`: searches, creates, updates, and safely deletes Google
  Calendar events.
- `task_management`: creates and verifies Google Tasks items.

The external backends are optional. The credential-free Demo uses deterministic
providers while exercising the real Harness control flow.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Quick Start with Docker
Requirements:

- Docker Desktop with Docker Compose
- Git

Start the Demo API and Redis:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up --build
```

The default `APP_MODE=demo` does not call OpenAI, Slack, Google, a log platform,
or a live knowledge backend.

Verify the service:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/health
```

Expected response:

```json
{"status":"ok","mode":"demo"}
```

Run an Agent request:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/agent/run \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"message":"Find the E102 incident procedure","session_id":"demo-user"}'
```

Interactive API documentation is available at
[`http://localhost:8000/docs`](http://localhost:8000/docs).

Stop the containers with `Ctrl+C`, or run:

```bash
docker compose stop
```

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Credential-Free Demo Scenarios
Five deterministic scenarios demonstrate the Harness behavior:

1. `knowledge`: runs the 100 -> 20 -> 3 retrieval flow and returns citations.
2. `log_to_task`: binds diagnosis output into a dependent task-creation step and
   verifies the external identifier.
3. `parallel_reads`: starts independent knowledge and calendar reads before
   either finishes.
4. `safe_delete`: requires confirmation, deletes once, and rejects confirmation
   replay.
5. `recovery`: resumes an interrupted `RUNNING` read step.

With Docker running, execute all scenarios inside the application container:

```bash
docker compose exec app python -m scripts.run_demo_scenarios \
  --output logs/demo_scenarios.json
```

The report is written to `logs/demo_scenarios.json`, and Workspace evidence is
written under `workspaces/demo-cli/`.

Individual scenarios are also available over HTTP:

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Credential-Free Demo Scenarios
```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/demo/scenarios
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/demo/scenarios/knowledge
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/demo/scenarios/log_to_task
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/demo/scenarios/parallel_reads
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/demo/scenarios/safe_delete
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/demo/scenarios/recovery
```

Each result includes the response, trace, and an `evidence_boundary` describing
what the deterministic scenario does and does not prove. See
[`docs/DEMO.md`](docs/DEMO.md) for details.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Local Development
The repository targets Python 3.12 and uses Poetry:

```bash
poetry env use 3.12
poetry install
cp .env.example .env
make test
make demo
```

Useful commands:

```bash
make test                    # Unit tests with no external services
make test-integration        # Local infrastructure integration tests
make demo                    # Deterministic credential-free API
make demo-scenarios          # All five deterministic Harness scenarios
make cli MESSAGE="Find E102" # Local CLI through the same Harness
make eval                    # Real-model routing evaluation
make test-live-read          # Read-only external integration probes
make test-live-write         # Explicit sandbox write probes and cleanup
make slack                   # Real Slack Socket Mode entry point
```

GitHub Actions runs the unit suite with Python 3.12 on every push and pull
request.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > State and Storage Model
The Harness separates operational state from evidence:

| Layer | Contents | Default retention |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Redis task/session | Step dependencies, statuses, external IDs, recent conversation | Task: 7 days; session: 24 hours |
| Workspace | Request, plan, step inputs and outputs, response evidence | Deployment-managed |
| Redis user profile | Explicit timezone, language, and default resource preferences | 30 days, renewable |

Workspace JSON is written atomically and referenced with SHA-256 and byte count.
Results larger than `WORKSPACE_INLINE_MAX_BYTES` remain in the Workspace and are
represented in Redis by `workspace://` references. Downstream `$from` bindings
can resolve those references transparently.

User preferences are explicit rather than inferred silently from conversation:

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > State and Storage Model
```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:8000/v1/users/demo-user/profile \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"user_id":"demo-user","time_zone":"America/New_York","output_language":"en"}'

curl http://localhost:8000/v1/users/demo-user/profile
```

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > RAG Retrieval and Optional Candidate Compression
The evaluated default knowledge pipeline in `src/harness/rag.py` uses:

```text
FAISS Top-5 -> multilingual Cross-Encoder Top-3 -> Answer
```

Set `RAG_RETRIEVAL_MODE=faiss` for the fast fallback:

```text
FAISS Top-3 -> Answer
```

Set `RAG_RETRIEVAL_MODE=full` to enable the experimental compression path:

```text
FAISS Top-100 -> SVMRank Top-20 -> Cross-Encoder Top-3 -> Answer
```

metadata.section: RAG Retrieval and Optional Candidate Compression
heading_path: RAG Retrieval and Optional Candidate Compression

content:
Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > RAG Retrieval and Optional Candidate Compression
- FAISS performs normalized-vector candidate recall.
- The default multilingual mMARCO Cross-Encoder and Top-5 window improved the
  checked-in holdout evaluation over FAISS alone. Its model revision is pinned
  in `.env.example` for reproducibility.
- SVMRank optionally reduces Cross-Encoder work using an offline-trained linear
  ranker. Keep it disabled until its candidate recall is validated on a
  representative holdout set.
- FAISS-only mode does not load Cross-Encoder or SVMRank artifacts, so it remains
  available as a low-latency and offline fallback.
- The Cross-Encoder scores all query-document pairs in one batch.
- The answer includes source references and per-stage retrieval metrics.
- If no candidate reaches `RAG_RELEVANCE_THRESHOLD`, the pipeline refuses to
  answer without calling the generator.

Install optional local retrieval and reranking dependencies:

metadata.section: RAG Retrieval and Optional Candidate Compression
heading_path: RAG Retrieval and Optional Candidate Compression

content:
Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > RAG Retrieval and Optional Candidate Compression
```bash
poetry install -E rag
```

Build an index from JSONL documents containing `chunk_id`, `content`, `source`,
and optional `metadata`:

```bash
make knowledge-chunks
make rag-index \
  INPUT=data/knowledge_chunks.jsonl \
  FAISS_INDEX_PATH=rag_data/knowledge.faiss \
  RAG_DOCUMENTS_PATH=rag_data/documents.jsonl
make rag-training-data
make rag-train
```

Evaluate retrieval ablations with a fixed dataset:

```bash
make rag-eval DATASET=evals/rag_cases.jsonl
```

Run one end-to-end query with the configured retrieval mode and generator:

```bash
python scripts/run_live_rag_query.py \
  "What are the three retrieval stages in the OpsFlow knowledge pipeline?" \
  --output logs/live_rag_query.json
```

metadata.section: RAG Retrieval and Optional Candidate Compression
heading_path: RAG Retrieval and Optional Candidate Compression

content:
Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > RAG Retrieval and Optional Candidate Compression
`RAG_RELEVANCE_THRESHOLD` is a Cross-Encoder logit threshold, not a
probability. Keep the default refusal behavior until the threshold has been
calibrated on a representative labeled dataset. For an explicit local
calibration experiment, pass `--threshold` to the live-query script.

Real embeddings, model downloads, trained artifacts, and generator calls are
Live Integration evidence; injected test doubles do not prove those external
systems are available.

content:
Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Live Integrations
Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and configure only the services you intend to
exercise:

- OpenAI-compatible routing and answer generation
- Embeddings and RAG artifacts
- Redis
- Slack Socket Mode
- Google Calendar and Tasks OAuth
- Log API

Run read-only checks separately from the deterministic suite:

```bash
make eval
make test-live-read
```

Every probe records `PASS`, `SKIP`, or `FAIL`. Missing credentials are reported
as `SKIP`, never as success. External writes remain disabled unless explicit
sandbox Calendar, Tasklist, or Slack Channel identifiers are configured and
`make test-live-write` is invoked. See
[`docs/LIVE_INTEGRATION.md`](docs/LIVE_INTEGRATION.md).

Never commit `.env`, `credentials.json`, `token.pickle`, real provider
responses, user content, runtime logs, or local databases.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Observability and Performance Reports
Trace events correlate routing, planning, execution, retries, verification,
latency, and errors for each request. Large or sensitive payloads stay in the
Workspace; Trace records their checksummed references.

Generate a scoped performance report after running a fixed dataset:

```bash
make perf-report \
  TRACE=logs/harness_trace.jsonl \
  DATASET=evals/router_cases.jsonl \
  CONCURRENCY=1 \
  WARM_STATE=prewarmed \
  MODEL=gpt-4o-mini \
  OUTPUT=logs/performance_report.json
```

The report records the dataset hash, request count, concurrency, warm state,
model, hardware, timestamp, Git commit, P50, P95, and failure rate. Performance
claims should be made only from a saved report with its stated test boundary.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Project Structure
```text
src/api.py                    REST entry point
src/SlackWebHook.py           Slack Socket Mode entry point
src/cli.py                    Local CLI entry point
src/agent_runtime.py          Shared runtime factory
src/HarnessAgent.py           Entry-point adapter
src/harness/application.py    Routing, planning, and task creation
src/harness/task_runner.py    Dependency scheduling and recovery
src/harness/runtime.py        Validation, retry, and write controls
src/harness/registry.py       Skill discovery and schemas
src/harness/rag.py            Three-stage retrieval pipeline
src/harness/workspace.py      Durable request and step evidence
src/harness/trace.py          Correlated execution events
src/harness/skills/           Canonical business skill contracts
scripts/                      Demo, evaluation, indexing, and reports
tests/                        Unit and focused integration tests
```

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness > Project Structure
The complete acceptance criteria and evidence boundaries are documented in
[`docs/FINAL_STATE_ACCEPTANCE.md`](docs/FINAL_STATE_ACCEPTANCE.md).

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness migration > Why this is a Harness
The legacy application attaches every LangChain tool directly to one
`AgentExecutor`. The new runtime places an explicit execution layer between the
model and business tools:

1. `SkillRegistry` discovers reusable capabilities without initializing them.
2. `LangChainRequestRouter` emits a schema-validated route or task plan.
3. `HarnessApplication` validates that planned skills are registered.
4. `SkillRuntime` validates inputs, isolates errors, records timing, and emits
   trace events.
5. `TaskRunner` executes multi-step plans only when dependencies are complete.
6. `RedisTaskStore` persists task and step state with a bounded TTL.
7. `RedisSessionStore` supplies a bounded recent-message window for follow-ups.
8. `JsonlTraceSink` preserves request-correlated routing and execution events.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness migration > Why this is a Harness
Trace events now carry the request/session/user/task/step correlation IDs. Raw
requests, plans, step inputs/outputs, and final responses remain in Workspace;
the trace contains their checksum-bearing references plus status, timing,
attempt count, verification state, and external resource IDs. Recovery emits
separate start/completion events. `scripts/summarize_performance.py` derives
request-level P50/P95/failure rate while recording dataset hash, concurrency,
warm state, model, hardware, timestamp, and Git commit.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness migration > Why this is a Harness
Task control state and durable execution evidence are intentionally separated.
Redis stores the compact task graph, current status, verification metadata, and
bounded session context. `LocalWorkspace` stores `request.json`, `plan.json`,
and each step's input/output JSON with a checksum-bearing reference. Results
larger than `WORKSPACE_INLINE_MAX_BYTES` are omitted from the Redis task payload
and loaded from Workspace when a downstream `$from` binding needs them.

Cross-session preferences use a third namespace, `RedisUserProfileStore`, keyed
by `user_id`. The REST profile endpoints explicitly manage time zone, output
language, default Calendar/Tasks targets, and user preferences. Profiles are
passed to the Router as system context; the Harness does not infer or mutate
them from ordinary conversation.

Multi-step plans can bind a downstream argument to a declared upstream output:

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness migration > Why this is a Harness
```json
{"subject": {"$from": "diagnose.output.issue_title"}}
```

The application validates the source output schema before execution, and the
TaskRunner stores the resolved arguments with the step state.

Independent `read` steps in the same ready batch run concurrently. Global
concurrency defaults to four workers through `HARNESS_MAX_CONCURRENCY`; each
Skill also declares its own concurrency limit and timeout. Write operations
remain serial. A failed or timed-out independent read does not erase successful
results from the same batch.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness migration > Why this is a Harness
Side-effecting steps always run through TaskState, including single-step writes.
Before execution the runner persists an idempotency record. A write becomes
complete only after its Skill verifier confirms external state and returns an
external resource ID. An indeterminate result becomes `UNKNOWN` and is never
blindly replayed. `recover(task_id)` safely reruns interrupted reads, reuses
verified idempotency records, and re-verifies unknown writes. Only read Skills
use automatic bounded retries; non-idempotent writes execute once.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness migration > Migration boundary
The Harness is now the default runtime for Slack, the REST API, and the local
CLI. All three adapters build their runtime through `src.agent_runtime` and use
the same `run_agent(input, session_id)` contract. The old `AgentClass` remains
available only as a temporary, explicit `AGENT_RUNTIME=legacy` fallback.

Unit tests prove the Harness control flow, but live checks for Qdrant, Redis,
the configured LLM, Slack, Google Calendar, and Google Tasks remain separate
integration evidence.

The checked-in Workspace backend is a local filesystem implementation suitable
for direct reproduction and one-node deployment. Shared object storage,
retention jobs, encryption policy, and live Redis durability remain deployment
integration work rather than unit-test claims.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness migration > Implemented skills
| Skill | Current backend | Operation type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `knowledge_search` | FAISS → SVMRank → Cross-Encoder → grounded LLM | Read |
| `log_diagnosis` | Configured log API or supplied log text | Read |
| `web_search` | Existing SerpAPI tool | Read |
| `calendar_management` | Existing Google Calendar tools | Read and write |
| `task_management` | Existing Google Tasks create tool | Write |

`src/harness/skills` is the canonical Skill system used by the Harness. The
older `src/skills` package is retained only by the explicit legacy runtime.
`log_diagnosis` is registered and covered with injected-backend tests; a live
log-platform result must still be reported separately from those tests.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness migration > Verification
Run:

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The focused suite covers Skill registration, schema validation, Runtime error
normalization, dependency validation, state transitions, Redis serialization,
request routing, task execution, session isolation, and trace persistence.

Title: Credential-free final-state demo > Run
```bash
cp .env.example .env
make demo-scenarios
```

This command requires no external credentials. It runs the production Harness
control path with deterministic routing and injected Mock providers. The raw
result is saved to `logs/demo_scenarios.json`; request, plan, input, output, and
response artifacts are saved below `workspaces/demo-cli/`.

Title: Credential-free final-state demo > What each scenario proves
| Scenario | Evidence produced | Explicit boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `knowledge` | 100/20/3 retrieval counts, grounded answer, chunk sources | Fixed local documents and answerer; no external embedding or LLM call |
| `log_to_task` | DAG, output binding, Mock Task ID and verified write | Mock log and task providers |
| `parallel_reads` | Both Skill start events occur before either completion | Fixed local delays, not a production load test |
| `safe_delete` | Candidate lookup, expiring pending confirmation, verified delete, replay rejection | In-process Mock Calendar; not session-bound Google evidence |
| `recovery` | Interrupted read reset, re-execution and recovery events | In-memory state; Redis process restart is a separate integration test |

Title: Credential-free final-state demo > Inspect evidence
Each scenario result contains `request_ids`, `responses`, `trace`, and an
`evidence_boundary`. Workspace references in the Trace point to the exact JSON
files used by the run and include SHA-256 checksums.

To use the HTTP presentation instead:

```bash
make demo
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/demo/scenarios/knowledge
```

Docker Compose starts the same credential-free API by default:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

Do not describe these runs as OpenAI, Google Calendar, Google Tasks, Redis
restart, Slack, or log-platform live integration. Those require separately
recorded runs with the corresponding services configured.

Title: Live integration evidence
Live checks are intentionally separate from unit tests and the deterministic
Demo. Never commit `.env`, OAuth tokens, API keys, raw provider responses, or
real user content.

Title: Live integration evidence > Commands
```bash
make eval
make test-live-read
```

`make eval` calls the configured model but executes no Skill. The current fixed
dataset contains five cases each for Knowledge, Log Diagnosis, Calendar, and
Tasks. Detailed per-case results are written to
`logs/router_evaluation.jsonl`.

`make test-live-read` writes `logs/live_integrations.json`. Every probe is one
of:

- `PASS`: the configured external system responded and the stated assertion
  was verified;
- `SKIP`: credentials, artifacts, sandbox identifiers, or a local service are
  absent;
- `FAIL`: the service was configured but the probe failed.

The runner never prints secret values or provider response bodies. Failures
record only the exception type.

Title: Live integration evidence > Read probes
| Probe | What it verifies | Required configuration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI Router | Latest real-model fixed-dataset results all passed | `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `BASE_MODEL`, then `make eval` |
| Redis | `PING`; optional scoped key round-trip only in write mode | running `REDIS_URL` |
| Log API | Time-bounded HTTP GET and JSON response | `LOG_API_URL`, `LIVE_LOG_*` query fields |
| RAG retrieval | Embedding → FAISS → SVMRank → Cross-Encoder | three RAG artifacts and `LIVE_RAG_QUERY` |
| Google read | Lists at most one Calendar and one Tasklist | local valid `token.pickle` |
| Slack auth | Slack `auth.test` | `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` |

Title: Live integration evidence > External write probes
Writes require both the `--allow-writes` flag used by `make test-live-write`
and explicit sandbox target IDs:

```env
LIVE_GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID=
LIVE_GOOGLE_TASKLIST_ID=
LIVE_SLACK_CHANNEL_ID=
```

Google creates a temporary Event and Task, reads both back, records their
external IDs, and deletes them in a `finally` cleanup. Slack posts one clearly
labelled probe message; it is externally visible and is not run by default.

Title: Live integration evidence > Current verified snapshot — 2026-11-07
- OpenAI Router: `PASS`, 20/20 on the final four core Skill classes.
- Redis: `FAIL`, URL configured but no Redis server is running locally.
- Log API: `SKIP`, endpoint not configured.
- RAG retrieval: `SKIP`, FAISS/documents/SVMRank artifacts absent.
- Google Calendar/Tasks: `SKIP`, OAuth token absent.
- Slack: `SKIP`, tokens absent.

The raw reports are under ignored `logs/`. This snapshot proves only model
routing. It does not prove Skill execution, provider writes, Slack Socket Mode,
Redis restart recovery, or end-to-end production behavior.

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准 > 1. 文档目的
本文档定义本项目从当前原型演进到简历最终态时必须满足的验收标准。
后续实现、测试、演示和 GitHub 发布均以本文档为统一基线。

项目的最终目标是提供一个可以从 GitHub 克隆、按文档直接启动、能够展示真实
Agent 执行过程，并且具备测试、评测、Trace 和可复现实验结果的完整项目。

heading_path: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准

content:
Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准 > 2. 最终态系统边界
最终主链路为：

```text
Slack / Local Demo / REST API
              ↓
      FastAPI + Adapter
              ↓
      OpsFlow Agent Harness
  Router → Planner → TaskRunner → Runtime
              ↓
            Skills
  Knowledge / Log Diagnosis / Calendar / Tasks
```

配套组件：

- Redis：保存 Session、Task、Step、幂等记录和外部对象 ID；
- Workspace：保存原始日志、检索证据、工具材料和步骤输出；
- Trace：记录路由、计划、执行、延迟、Token、错误和验证结果；
- LLM：负责请求理解、规划和基于证据的内容生成；
- Harness：负责状态、依赖、执行控制、恢复和安全边界；
- Skill：负责具体业务能力及外部状态验证。

核心责任边界：

> 模型负责理解和规划，Harness 负责状态和执行控制，Skill 负责具体业务操作。

heading_path: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准

content:
Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准 > 3. 统一完成定义
某项能力只有同时满足以下条件，才可以标记为“已完成”：

1. 代码已经接入默认 Harness 主链路，不是孤立脚本或未注册模块；
2. 输入和输出具有明确 Schema；
3. 关键成功、失败和边界行为具有单元测试；
4. 涉及基础设施时具有可重复的集成测试；
5. 涉及真实外部服务时具有单独记录的 Live Integration 结果；
6. Trace 可以还原该能力的关键执行过程；
7. README 或对应文档提供可执行的复现命令；
8. 测试结论能够追溯到测试环境、原始输出和 Git commit。

以下证据不能相互替代：

- 单元测试通过不等于真实外部服务联调通过；
- Mock/Fake Backend 通过不等于 Live Integration 通过；
- 路由正确不等于 Skill 执行成功；
- Skill 返回成功不等于外部状态已经验证成功；
- 固定预热测试的性能数据不代表通用线上 SLA。

heading_path: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准

content:
Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准 > 4. 必须通过的最终 Demo 场景 > 场景 A：带证据的知识库问答
示例请求：

```text
从内部知识库查一下 E102 错误怎么处理？
```

预期执行：

```text
Router
→ Knowledge Skill
→ FAISS Top-100
→ SVMRank Top-20
→ BERT Cross-Encoder Top-3
→ LLM 基于证据回答
```

验收条件：

- Router 只选择 `knowledge_search`；
- 返回答案以及可定位的来源文档或 Chunk；
- Trace 记录三层检索的候选数量和各阶段耗时；
- 最终回答只能使用选中的证据；
- 没有相关证据时明确拒答，不生成无依据答案；
- 能运行 FAISS、FAISS + SVMRank、FAISS + Cross-Encoder 和完整三级检索的消融评测；
- CPU 环境可以运行缩小版 Demo，GPU 仅作为可选加速。

所需证据：

- 单元测试；
- 固定数据集上的 Recall、MRR 或 NDCG；
- 一次可复现的端到端查询；
- 示例 Trace 和最终回答。

示例请求：

```text
step_1: log_diagnosis
step_2: task_management, depends_on=[step_1]
```

- `log_diagnosis` 已注册到默认 Skill Registry；
- 第二步通过显式输出引用读取第一步的结构化结果；
- 第一步没有发现目标问题时，不创建任务；
- 第一步失败时，第二步保持阻断状态；
- 创建后保存外部 Task ID，并查询外部系统验证结果；
- Trace 能还原计划、输入绑定、执行结果和验证结果。

- 输出绑定单元测试；
- 日志 API 和任务 API 的集成测试；
- 一次真实或可重复沙箱环境的端到端演示；
- Workspace 中保存的日志证据和步骤输出。

示例请求：

```text
查询项目文档，同时检查我明天下午的日历。
```

预期计划：

```text
step_1: knowledge_search
step_2: calendar_management.check_availability
step_1 与 step_2 无依赖，可并行执行
```

验收条件：

- Planner 不创建虚假依赖；
- TaskRunner 并行执行同一批可运行的读取步骤；
- 系统具有全局和 Skill 级最大并发限制；
- 单步超时或失败不会破坏另一个独立步骤的结果；
- 最终响应能够聚合两个步骤的结果；
- Trace 的起止时间可以证明步骤确实重叠执行。

所需证据：

- 两个固定延迟 Skill 的并行测试；
- 串行与并行耗时对比；
- 超时、取消和部分失败测试；
- 示例并行 Trace。

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准 > 4. 必须通过的最终 Demo 场景 > 场景 D：需要确认的安全写操作
示例请求：

```text
帮我删除明天下午的项目评审会议。
```

预期执行：

```text
查询候选会议
→ 返回候选对象和 event_id
→ 请求用户确认
→ 用户明确确认
→ 执行删除
→ 查询 Calendar 验证删除结果
```

验收条件：

- 未得到明确确认时不执行删除；
- 确认内容与待删除对象、用户和会话绑定；
- 确认具有有效期，过期后必须重新确认；
- 重复提交同一确认不会重复执行；
- 写操作保存幂等键和外部 event ID；
- 网络超时后先验证外部状态，不盲目重复删除；
- Trace 记录确认、执行和验证三个独立阶段。

所需证据：

- 未确认、错误确认、过期确认和重复确认测试；
- Google Calendar Fake Backend 集成测试；
- 独立记录的 Live Integration；
- 删除前后外部状态证据。

Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准 > 4. 必须通过的最终 Demo 场景 > 场景 E：进程中断后的任务恢复
演示条件：任务执行到中间步骤时主动终止进程。

验收条件：

- 重启后能够从 Redis 读取未终结任务；
- 已经验证成功的步骤不会重复执行；
- 安全且未完成的步骤可以继续执行；
- 遗留 `RUNNING` 步骤不会永久卡住任务；
- 结果不明确的写操作进入 `UNKNOWN`；
- `UNKNOWN` 步骤先检查外部状态，再决定成功、失败或重试；
- 恢复过程本身写入 Trace；
- 最终状态与外部系统实际状态一致。

所需证据：

- 中断恢复集成测试；
- 写操作成功但响应超时的测试；
- 重启前后的 Redis 状态快照；
- 恢复过程 Trace 和外部状态验证结果。

content:
Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准 > 5. 状态和数据约定
任务步骤至少支持以下状态：

```text
PENDING
READY
RUNNING
SUCCEEDED
FAILED
RETRYABLE
UNKNOWN
BLOCKED
CANCELLED
```

数据分层要求：

- `session_id`：最近对话和当前澄清上下文；
- `task_id`：计划、步骤、依赖、状态、幂等键和外部对象 ID；
- `user_id`：跨会话偏好，例如时区和默认日历；
- Redis：保存状态、短期上下文和引用；
- Workspace：保存原始材料、证据和大型步骤输出；
- Trace：保存执行事件和可观测性字段。

重要业务结果不得只存在于具有 TTL 的 Redis Key 中。

heading_path: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准

content:
Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准 > 6. 可观测性验收
给定一个 `request_id`，系统必须能够还原：

```text
用户请求
→ 使用的上下文
→ Router/Planner 决策
→ Task DAG
→ 每一步输入和输出引用
→ Skill 执行状态
→ 外部对象 ID
→ 外部验证结果
→ 最终响应
```

Trace 至少记录：

- `request_id`、`session_id`、`task_id`、`step_id`；
- 模型和 Skill 名称；
- 开始时间、结束时间和持续时间；
- 路由和计划结果；
- Token 用量；
- 错误码、重试次数和恢复动作；
- 外部对象 ID；
- Workspace Evidence 引用；
- 外部状态验证结果。

任何性能指标必须同时记录：

- 测试数据集；
- 请求数量和并发度；
- 冷启动或预热状态；
- 模型和硬件配置；
- P50、P95 和失败率；
- 测试时间和对应 Git commit。

heading_path: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准

content:
Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准 > 7. GitHub 可复现验收
首次使用者应能根据 README 完成：

```bash
git clone <repository>
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up --build
```

项目必须提供：

- 不需要真实凭据的 Mock/Demo 模式；
- 可选的 Slack、OpenAI、Google 和日志平台 Live 模式；
- 固定的示例数据和评测数据；
- 单元测试、集成测试、评测和 Demo 的独立命令；
- GitHub Actions；
- 架构、Demo、评测和安全配置文档；
- 不包含密钥、OAuth Token 或用户隐私数据的示例 Trace。

建议统一命令：

```text
make test
make test-integration
make eval
make demo
```

content:

- [ ] Harness 是默认且唯一的正式执行主链路；
- [ ] Knowledge、Log Diagnosis、Calendar、Tasks 四类核心 Skill 已注册；

- [ ] Redis、Workspace、User Profile 和 Trace 边界清晰；
- [ ] 三级 RAG 及其消融评测可复现；
- [ ] 五个最终 Demo 场景全部通过；
- [ ] 单元、集成、Live 和端到端证据分别记录；
- [ ] 本地 Demo 可以展示计划、步骤、证据和 Trace；
- [ ] Slack Demo 可以展示真实业务操作；
- [ ] Docker 和 README 支持从 GitHub 直接复现；
- [ ] 所有公开指标均可追溯到原始结果和 Git commit；
- [ ] 仓库中不存在密钥、Token 或真实用户隐私数据。

content:
Title: OpsFlow Agent Harness 最终态验收标准 > 9. 当前不作为第一阶段完成条件的内容
以下能力可以在五个核心场景稳定后再扩展，不阻塞当前最终态验收：

- 多租户权限系统；
- Kubernetes 部署；
- 多区域容灾；
- 高并发生产 SLA；
- 自定义模型训练；
- 大规模在线学习；
- 复杂管理后台；
- 除四个核心 Skill 外的大量第三方集成。

这些能力不应提前引入，以免扩大当前项目范围。
